## Working Read

This essay turns the self into a system of internal standing rather than a single sovereign voice. Its central diagnosis is that cost is often made invisible by assigning it to the body, memory, feeling, desire, or future self while the conscious account records only output.

The self becomes coherent when its parts remain legible, negotiable, and returnable without one part being permanently converted into fuel for another. The essay therefore links acceptance, consent, witness, delayed feedback, and repair: internal coherence is constitutional participation, not uniformity.

## Core Claim

The self can continue becoming only when its parts retain standing and can consent to continue; coherence is negotiated integration, not the victory of one internal signal.

## Key Ideas

- The self is a constitutional relationship among partially distinct processes.
- Standing precedes performance; a signal does not lose standing when capacity falls.
- Hidden internal costs return as delayed feedback.
- Positive loops generate capacity while negative loops regulate deviation.
- A negative loop can preserve life without becoming a life.
- Identity stores expenditure and closes some possibilities while opening others.

## Cost Series

This essay is the inward scale of the Cost series: [Self](../the-cost-of-self/index.md) → [Family](../the-cost-of-family/index.md) → [Community](../the-cost-of-community/index.md) → [Earth](../the-cost-of-earth/index.md) → [Cosmos](../the-cost-of-cosmos/index.md).

## Open Questions

- What internal signals are being treated as externalities in the present account of the self?
- When does regulation become hidden extraction rather than care?
- How can future-self standing be represented in present decisions?
- What forms of repair restore capacity without pretending that expenditure did not occur?
